content_of_post_to_comment:
Started it as a bit of a joke, honestly. I work early morning shifts so my brain is basically oatmeal by 6am, and I figured if I just wrote three sentences before bed it would count as a personality trait I could mention at parties. Low bar. Very on brand.

But something shifted around week three. Not dramatically, not in a podcastworthy epiphany kind of way. More like I started noticing when I was just coasting through the day versus actually being present in it. The walk to work. The first pour of the morning. Conversations I was halflistening to.

The journalling did not fix anything. I still forget things, still get in my head, still have weeks where I feel like I am running two steps behind everyone else. But there is something about writing it down that makes the day feel less like something happening to you and more like something you are actually in.

90 days is not a long time. But I also kind of cannot imagine stopping now.

Curious if anyone else has picked up a small habit that ended up doing more than you expected it to. Not the big dramatic life overhauls, just the quiet stuff that compounds slowly.
comment: The part about noticing when you were coasting really hits on why tiny habits can stick. I’ve found journaling works less like a solution and more like a checkpoint that catches patterns you’d normally miss. Sometimes the value is just creating a little space between having a day and actually experiencing it.
